title: Relay.app Free Plan: Limits and Alternatives (2026)
summary: Relay.app free plan has monthly limits that shut down automations mid-operation. Find out those limits and whether you need to upgrade or switch tools.
body_markdown:
## What the stalled Relay.app workflows cost the team


When a workflow stalls, **you lose three things you can count** : hours someone spends doing the work by hand, records that sit unprocessed, and customers who wait for an answer.


When a workflow stops, the work doesn't disappear. Someone on your team picks it up by hand, usually the person least able to spare the time. The real cost is that person's day, plus the slower work they pushed aside to do it.


Look at published estimates of small-business downtime to see how widely that cost can swing. According to[Texmg](https://texmg.com/resources/real-cost-it-downtime-houston-small-businesses) , they run from about $2,800–3,000 an hour for a 30-person firm, so the financial case for preventing downtime is not optional.


A broader small-business range runs from $3,362 at the low end to $25,620 at the high end, with $10,000 quoted as an "up to" figure.


Because the gap between low and high is wide, your own number depends on what the stalled work touches. A paused internal reminder sits near the bottom, and a paused order or billing step sits much higher.


Those figures describe downtime in general, not Relay.app. Multiply the hours your team spends catching up by what those hours cost you, and you have a number that belongs to your business.


### Records and customers hit by stalled workflows


Each stalled run leaves something unfinished: a lead not routed, a form not logged, an update not sent. Those records stay in limbo until someone notices, and noticing usually takes longer than the stop itself.


Customers feel it as waiting. They don't know a plan limit exists. They know their request went quiet, and a quiet request reads as a company that doesn't answer. That's the hardest cost to win back, and it grows the longer the stop goes unnoticed.


So count two things for your own setup: how many records one stalled day leaves behind, and how many of those belong to a person waiting on you. Together with the catch-up hours, they tell you what staying put really costs.
